- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model should not underestimate price spike potential — increase forecast baseline by 3–8% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 75), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish swings (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 → 1.00), model should not assume linear trend — apply mean reversion to 3–5 day moving average of recent prices.
- When bullish events outnumber bearish (net bullish > 0), model should not ignore sentiment — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment > 0.75.
- If model forecast is flat (±0.1% over 5 days) and true outcome shows volatility, assume model is underfitting — increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model should not assume price will stabilize — expect 2–4% upward bias for first 7–10 days, then gradual mean reversion.
